description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of cognitive and affective alexithymia dimensions during emotion perception and emotion regulation in healthy subjects using fMRI.

spans.text: The aim of the current study was to investigate the neural correlates underlying the two alexithymia dimensions during emotion perception and emotion regulation.

value: We suggest that during the first two phases of emotion processing, the cognitive alexithymia dimension will be associated with decreased activation in brain areas involved in the identification of emotions (such as the amygdala) while the affective dimension is proposed to be associated with activation in areas involved in emotional awareness (such as the ACC).
During reappraisal we expect to find lower activation in the dorsal system (e.g. DLPFC) associated with the cognitive dimension, as reappraisal can be seen as a cognitive task.

The emotion regulation task [adapted from ( Ochsner and Gross, 2005 )] consisted of four conditions, Attend Neutral, Attend Negative, Reappraise and Suppress.

description.value: Participants viewed negative or neutral pictures and then attended to, reappraised, or suppressed the emotional content.

spans.text: The task consisted of an emotion perception part in which subjects viewed negative or neutral pictures, followed by an emotion regulation part where subjects were instructed to either attend to, reappraise or suppress the emotional content of the picture.
Attend Neutral
The 22 neutral pictures were always paired with the ‘attend’ instruction.

description.value: Participants viewed neutral pictures and attended closely to them without changing how they felt. Neutral pictures were always paired with the attend instruction.

spans.text: During attend, participants just had to look closely at the picture and not change the way they were feeling.

description.value: Participants reappraised negative pictures so that they became less emotionally disturbing.

spans.text: Reappraise meant that the participants had to reappraise the picture in such a way that it became less emotionally disturbing.
Suppress
Negative pictures could be paired with either reappraise (22 pictures), suppress (22 pictures) or attend (22 pictures).

description.value: Participants suppressed emotional expression while viewing negative pictures, refraining from expressing emotions so that bystanders could not read their emotions from their face.
